text: Christianity began almost 2,000 years ago with Jesus of Nazareth, a Jewish teacher from Galilee.
According to the Gospels, he taught about the kingdom of God and was put to death on a cross in Jerusalem.
src: Christianity began with Jesus of Nazareth, a Jewish teacher from Galilee / Roman Judea and Galilee, about 30 CE
Most of what is known of him comes from the Gospels / proclaiming the coming kingdom of God, and that he was crucified in Jerusalem

text: His followers believed that he rose from the dead and was the Messiah, promised in the Jewish scriptures.
Christians share bread and wine in memory of Jesus' last supper, in a meal called the Eucharist.
src: His followers proclaimed that he had risen from the dead and appeared to them, and that he was the Messiah, the Christ, promised in the Jewish scriptures
the Eucharist, also called Holy Communion or the Mass, the shared meal of bread and wine in memory of Jesus’ last supper

text: Apostles such as Paul and Peter carried the faith across the Roman Empire, as far as Rome.
Roman rulers sometimes punished Christians, because they refused to honour the empire's gods.
src: Spread by apostles such as Paul across the Roman Empire / Paul was executed in Rome, by tradition under Nero, as was Peter
viewed with suspicion by Roman authorities for refusing to honour the gods of the state and the emperor / attempted to suppress it across the empire

text: Later the emperor Constantine let Christians worship freely, and it became the religion of the empire.
In 325 church leaders met at Nicaea and set out their main beliefs in the Nicene Creed.
src: in 313 he and his co-emperor Licinius granted Christians freedom of worship / In 380 Theodosius I made Nicene Christianity the official religion of the empire
325: The Council of Nicaea, called by Constantine, defines the faith in the Nicene Creed

text: Christians read the Bible, which has two parts, the Old Testament and the New Testament.
It has been translated into more languages than any other book.
src: The Christian Bible has two parts / the Old Testament (the Hebrew Bible, with further books in some churches) and the New Testament
The Bible has been translated, in whole or in part, into more languages than any other book

text: Christians built great churches, like Hagia Sophia, finished almost 1,500 years ago.
Today more than two billion people are Christians, more than follow any other religion.
src: Christian architecture produced Hagia Sophia, completed in 537
today about 2.3 billion people are Christians / the largest religion in the world
